## Purpose and selected system

Calculate how an explicit linear RLC network changes the modes of the selected
through-CPW and short–open meander resonator assembly. Preserve the launcher
variant's coupling geometry and 17 airbridges. Its reproducible public source
is being integrated with this notebook suite; these pages do not claim it is
already published.

This is a loaded electromagnetic mode problem, not automatic Josephson
nonlinearity or EPR analysis.

## Model, support and boundary choices

Use the notebook's exact conductor, substrate, bridge-deck/post and vacuum
model. Keep physical contact identity and Z separate from the nonmetal support
sheet. A named neutral support locates the electrical treatment; it is not
positive metal and does not create a galvanic short.

Select Series or Parallel topology and R, L and C independently. `None`
disables a branch; zero is a selected value, not a disabling convention.
Keep the support/contact normal distinct from the directed current line.
Terminal owners, load units and exterior treatment must be explicit.

Mode search, mesh, adaptation and field-saving choices belong to the concrete
notebook. They are calculation settings, not a new accuracy or design Gate.

## Workflow

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Palace

A Palace loaded-mode comparison must state its own physical load and boundary
treatment. The [SimplePad Palace LC notebook](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/SimplePad/palace_eigenmode.ipynb)
illustrates a separately authored inductive model; it is not the selected
assembly or a substitution for its general RLC network.

### AEDT

Use [CPW–meander RLC Eigenmode](../../notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CpwMeanderAirbridge/aedt_hfss_eigenmode_rlc.ipynb).
Construct the selected source, bind the support and electrical treatment,
inspect their native placement and values, and solve the loaded modes.
Analyze the returned run separately.

:::

## Expected outputs

Retain native support/contact readback, Series/Parallel treatment and enabled
branches, applied setup and adaptive history. Return mode frequencies and
requested saved fields with the exact load identity. Any native loss/Q output
must retain its physical interpretation.

::: {.callout-note}
A generic RLC treatment does not create a Josephson junction or an EPR
contribution. Use [EPR and loss](epr-loss.qmd) for that separate analysis purpose.
:::

See [source ownership](../tools/source-ownership.qmd),
